extraction.name: Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models
extraction.description: Introduces IFEval, a benchmark for evaluating instruction-following ability of LLMs using verifiable instructions.
extraction.creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Prompts were generated using few-shot prompting and manual curation. Base prompts were created with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions appended, then illogical prompts were removed via few-shot prompting, rephrased for diversity, and manually checked.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The dataset consists of 541 prompts, each containing one or more verifiable instructions from a set of 25 types.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Prompts were generated via few-shot prompting and manual curation. Illogical prompts were removed, and prompts were rephrased for diversity.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Verifiable instructions are defined as instructions amenable to objective verification of compliance. Verification is done using simple heuristics and programming, with a loose accuracy metric that applies transformations to reduce false negatives.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Loose accuracy metric uses transformations (e.g., removing markdown, first/last lines) to reduce false negatives, but may introduce false positives.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current implementation can be improved by increasing diversity and quantity of verifiable instructions, and extending to multi-modal use cases.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation of instruction-following ability of large language models.
